new_page.title: RRSP Home Buyers' Plan: $60,000 Limit & When You Repay (2026)
new_page.h1: How much can I take from my RRSP to buy a home?
new_page.description: The Home Buyers' Plan lets first-time buyers take up to $60,000 from their RRSPs, tax-free, and repay it over 15 years. Repayments start in the fifth year.

breadcrumbs.name: How much can I take from my RRSP to buy a home?

faq.q: Do I have to be a first-time buyer to use the Home Buyers' Plan?
faq.a: Generally yes, under the CRA's definition, though there are exceptions such as after a marriage or common-law breakdown, and for buying a home for a person with a disability.

faq.q: Can I use RRSP money I deposited last week?
faq.a: Money must be in the RRSP for at least 90 days before you withdraw it under the plan, or it may not be deductible.

parts.t: Up to $60,000 each under the Home Buyers' Plan (HBP), so $120,000 for a couple who both qualify. The withdrawal is not taxed, and you repay it to your RRSP over 15 years. For withdrawals made from 2022 to 2028, repayments start in the fifth year after the first withdrawal.

You withdraw from your RRSPs to buy or build a qualifying home for yourself (or for a related person with a disability). Each year you repay at least one-fifteenth; anything you skip is added to your income for that year.
Take $60,000 in 2026. Repayments start in 2030 at $4,000 a year ($60,000 ÷ 15) and finish in 2044.
The HBP and the First Home Savings Account can be used on the same purchase, which is how many couples in South Surrey and Langley reach a 10% to 20% down payment.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
